chapter: Dancers, Newton, Chu Berry and the Cab Calloway band
title: Cab bandmates: Dizzy, Milt Hinton, Hilton Jefferson, Jerry Blake

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Let's talk about some of the people on there. We talked about Chu already and we kind of touched on Dizzy, but anything else stand out about Dizzy?

No, I know that when Dizzy joined the band, I really loved Dizzy's playing because then he played to me exactly like Roy Eldridge and I just loved the way Roy played and Dizzy sounded exactly like Roy to me with the exception of a few little things that Dizzy used to do. But I liked Dizzy's playing. Milt Henton, very good bass player, there's another boy in there by the name of Hilton Jefferson.
Yes. Very good. He made a recording there with Cab, 'Willow Weep for Me', Jimmy Dorsey.
Jimmy Dorsey was just crazy about it.
Did you know Hilton very well?
He never went on to get the success something like Willie Smith.

No, no, he was a very quiet sort of a fellow, but very, I don't know, he had a subdued way about him, he never said much, you know, and very quiet, wasn't aggressive no kind of way you know, just very quiet, very nice. Everybody just loved Jeff, they called him, ongoing,
you know and just always quiet and could play that alto saxophone though.
Yeah, yeah. Hilton Jefferson, then there was Jerry Blake, he was in that band.
Second alto. He was the clarinet soloist.
Apparently what Jerry Blake, let me just check this to make sure, but he ended up in a mental institution.
Is he? I haven't heard or seen of him since I left the band.
I think I--suffered mental breakdown and spent many years in a sanitorium where he died in 1961.
Oh he died, huh. I didn't know that. In 1961.
